newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU grain crop jumps above 200 million tonnes.
newsitem.headline: EU grain crop jumps above 200 million tonnes.

text.p: The European Union forecast on Wednesday a bumper grain crop of 200.7 million tonnes in 1996, up 23 million tonnes from last year, following an increase in plantings, higher yields and favourable weather.
EU farmers, encouraged by record world prices and a relaxation in EU planting rules, expanded the cereals area by nearly four percent while yields rose nine percent to 5.4 tonnes per hectare.

The EU, which late last year taxed grain exports in order to ensure adequate supplies for domestic consumers after world prices soared above EU levels for the first time in two decades, is now about to restore wheat export subsidies.
With big harvests rolling in from the U.S., Canada and other major grain producing countries, world prices have fallen from record levels earlier this year and are now below EU levels.

In its latest estimates, the EU's executive Commission put the soft wheat crop in the 15 member states 10 percent higher at 88.7 million tonnes and the barley production a massive 20 percent bigger at 52.7 million tonnes.

The maize crop, which is still being harvested, is expected to rise 13 percent to 33.8 million tonnes while durum wheat, used for pasta and biscuits, is expected to soar 22 percent to 8.4 million tonnes.
The balance is made up of rye, sorghum and other coarse grains used mainly to feed animals.
